framework: New Mexico state academic standards: Physical Education
subject: Physical Education

source.publisher: New Mexico state education agency (machine-readable via Common Standards Project / ASN)

units.title: Demonstrates competency in many movement forms and proficiency in a few movement forms. Students will:

topics.title: Demonstrate proficiency in combining basic skills for participating in a variety of physical fitness activities: aquatics, dance, outdoor pursuits, individual activities/sports and team activities/sports:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate proficiency in combining basic skills for participating in a variety of physical fitness activities: aquatics, dance, outdoor pursuits, individual activities/sports and team activities/sports:

outcomes.text: Using basic team sport skills, students will reproduce sequences of combined skills in practice situations and modified games (i.e., basketball: pivot and shoot; receive a pass and dribble; soccer: receive and control; dribble and shoot; baseball/softball: run and slide; catch and throw, etc.); and

Using basic individual activity skills, students will reproduce sequences of combined skills in practice situations and modified activities (i.e., table tennis: stance, grip, serve, return-forehand/backhand; aerobic: in rhythm high step, squat step, boxes, grapevine, low march; roller blades: stand up, "V" push, turn, stop, etc.).

topics.title: Demonstrate proficiency using basic offensive and defensive strategies while playing a modified version of a learned team and individual sport:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate proficiency using basic offensive and defensive strategies while playing a modified version of a learned team and individual sport:

outcomes.text: For team sports, in a practice situation, defensive players will show and maintain proper position and techniques while offensive players use practiced plays and deception to attempt to move to open space; and

For dual sports, during practice and game situations, students will reproduce sequences of basic techniques and skills consisting of: foot work, court position, offensive and defensive strokes, placement of projectile and court position in relation to partner.

units.title: Applies movement concepts and principles to the learning and development of motor skills. Students will:

topics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of the concepts of body, effort, space and relationships in movement:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of the concepts of body, effort, space and relationships in movement:

outcomes.text: Describe how changing effort affects the outcome of a sport skill (i.e., tennis: smash versus lob; basketball: lay up versus three-point shot; track: long distance run versus sprint, etc.).

topics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of motor skills, motor behaviors and motor learning concepts in increasingly complex movement situations:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of motor skills, motor behaviors and motor learning concepts in increasingly complex movement situations:

outcomes.text: Use increasingly complex skills and movements to achieve the desired level of motor skill and performances (i.e., progress from dribbling without opposition to dribbling with opposition to dribbling in a game situation, etc.).

topics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of critical elements of fundamental and specialized movement skills:

subtopics.title: Demonstrate competency in the use of critical elements of fundamental and specialized movement skills:

outcomes.text: Apply knowledge of results to correct and improve future performance; and
Demonstrate ability to analyze a movement pattern by using knowledge of its critical elements (i.e., self-analysis and peer observation, etc.).

units.title: Exhibits knowledge and ability to participate in a physically active lifestyle. Students will:

topics.title: Be able to set personal physical activity goals and participate in individualized programs of physical activity and exercise:

subtopics.title: Be able to set personal physical activity goals and participate in individualized programs of physical activity and exercise:

outcomes.text: List and describe the benefits of setting personal fitness goals;
Maintain heart rate within the target heart rate zone (i.e., demonstrate proper technique of taking heart rate, explain target heart rate zone, etc.); and

Choose physical activities with the intent to improve and or maintain each of the following health-related fitness components: muscular strength (i.e., push-ups, thera-bands, weights, pull-ups, tumbling, etc.); endurance (i.e., running, aerobic activities, etc.); flexibility (i.e., stretching/warmup, cool-down activities, tumbling, etc.); cardiovascular (i.e., running and aerobic activities, etc.); body composition (i.e., toning activities, aerobic/anaerobic activities, weight training, etc.).

topics.title: Determine long-term benefits that may result from regular participation in physical activity:

subtopics.title: Determine long-term benefits that may result from regular participation in physical activity:

outcomes.text: Comprehend the benefits of physical activity (i.e., list and describe the health risks associated with an inactive lifestyle, list and describe the benefits of active lifestyles, etc.); and
Recognize the difference between anaerobic and aerobic fitness activities.

units.title: Achieves and maintains a health-enhancing level of physical fitness. Students will:

topics.title: Participate in physical activities that address each health-related physical fitness component:

subtopics.title: Participate in physical activities that address each health-related physical fitness component:

outcomes.text: Engage in appropriate physical activity that results in the development of cardiovascular endurance;
Select appropriate fitness activities that require muscular strength and muscular endurance;
Comprehend the benefits of flexibility; and
Explain the benefits of a healthy body composition.

topics.title: Assess personal fitness status within each health-related physical fitness component:

subtopics.title: Assess personal fitness status within each health-related physical fitness component:

outcomes.text: Comprehend personal fitness data and recognize individual strengths and weaknesses.

topics.title: Interpret the results of physical fitness assessments and use this information to develop individualized physical fitness goals with guidance from the teacher:

subtopics.title: Interpret the results of physical fitness assessments and use this information to develop individualized physical fitness goals with guidance from the teacher:

outcomes.text: Comprehend personal fitness data and recognize individual strengths and weaknesses; and
Choose appropriate physical activities to maintain and or improve strengths and weaknesses.

topics.title: Evaluate the effectiveness of exercise and other factors to obtain personal fitness goals:

subtopics.title: Evaluate the effectiveness of exercise and other factors to obtain personal fitness goals:

outcomes.text: Identify the components of a fitness program and apply them to personal fitness plans (i.e., include more aerobic activities, adjust sets and reps in strength programs, etc.).

units.title: Demonstrates responsible personal and social behavior in physical activity settings. Students will:

topics.title: Select and utilize safety principles in physical activity settings; grades 5-8 performance standards:

subtopics.title: Select and utilize safety principles in physical activity settings; grades 5-8 performance standards:

outcomes.text: Use equipment appropriately (i.e., use specific equipment for intended purposes, proper care and management of equipment, etc.);

Follow general classroom and specific activity rules (i.e., treat each other with respect, honor specific boundaries, use appropriate personal contact, positive response to teachers' instruction/comments, distinguish between compliance and non-compliance with rules and regulations and apply agreed-upon consequences when officiating, etc.); and

Follow established emergency procedures (i.e., first aid, fire drills, etc.); wear appropriate activity attire properly (i.e., shoes and socks, clothing specific to activity, clothing specific to school and district rules, no potentially harmful accessories, etc.).

topics.title: Exhibit appropriate personal and group conduct while engaging in physical activity:

subtopics.title: Exhibit appropriate personal and group conduct while engaging in physical activity:

outcomes.text: Identify a bullying situation and respond appropriately (i.e., refer to specific district "bully proofing" programs/parameters, go to a safe adult when in an unsafe situation, etc.);

Identify a sexual harassment situation and respond appropriately (i.e., refer to specific district regulations/policies, go to a safe adult when in an unsafe situation, demonstrate use of appropriate language and personal contact during physical activities, etc.); and
Accept responsibility for own actions and modify behaviors accordingly (i.e., take self out of negative situation, go to a safe adult in an unsafe situation, etc.).

topics.title: Recognize the influence of peer pressure and make appropriate decisions using problem-solving techniques to resolve conflict:

subtopics.title: Recognize the influence of peer pressure and make appropriate decisions using problem-solving techniques to resolve conflict:

outcomes.text: Identify/make positive choices in a variety of physical education settings (i.e., no teasing, name calling - use positive language, follow physical safety rules, follow all game/activity rules, etc.);
Recognize and ignore poor behavior choices of peers (i.e., identify bullying behaviors, identify sexual harassment behaviors, etc.);
List coping skills for dealing with negative behaviors (i.e., bully proofing, sexual harassment awareness, peer mediation, conflict resolution, etc.);
When in conflict, use appropriate problem-solving techniques (i.e., conflict mediation, cooperative discipline techniques, small group discussion/processing, etc.);

Identify and list components of sportsmanship (i.e., differentiate between positive and negative sportsmanship, fair play, respect referee's decision, understand importance of following rules, adhere to good sportsmanship concepts/ideas, etc.); and
Demonstrate ability to apply concepts of good sportsmanship (i.e., as participant, as spectator, as referee, as coach, etc.).

topics.title: Work cooperatively with a group to achieve group goals:

subtopics.title: Work cooperatively with a group to achieve group goals: (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Explain aspects of cooperative activities;
Participate positively in team building/cooperative activities;
Apply listening skills;
Explain different styles of leadership skills;

subtopics.title: Work cooperatively with a group to achieve group goals: (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Demonstrate importance of positive attitudes (i.e., communication, body language and listening skills, etc.);
Explain what it means to be a good team player; and
Analyze cause and effect during physical activities.

units.title: Demonstrates understanding and respect for differences among people in physical activity settings. Students will:

topics.title: Identify the contribution that physical activity plays in multicultural/ethnic awareness and in the acceptance of all peers:

subtopics.title: Identify the contribution that physical activity plays in multicultural/ethnic awareness and in the acceptance of all peers:

outcomes.text: Identify/explain the role of games, sports and dance in getting to know and understand various cultures; and
Distinguish the differences between varying cultures and their "native" sports/activities.
Research and present an unfamiliar game or dance from another country.

topics.title: Acknowledge all people of different gender, culture, ethnicity and disability and seek to learn more about both similarities and differences:

subtopics.title: Acknowledge all people of different gender, culture, ethnicity and disability and seek to learn more about both similarities and differences:

outcomes.text: Understand the need for game modifications to allow persons with special needs to participate;
Recognize the diverse attributes of age, race, ethnicity, gender and ability level and acknowledge how these differences can enhance group activities;
Participate in games/activities in which handicapping conditions are simulated (i.e., wheelchair basketball, etc.); and
Describe the social dynamics that occur when peers participate with partners in cooperative activities.

topics.title: Analyze how the media, particularly advertising, influences the perception of ideal body types:

subtopics.title: Analyze how the media, particularly advertising, influences the perception of ideal body types:

outcomes.text: Initiate discussion of media influences on behavior choices (i.e., print, radio, TV, etc.);
Explain/describe how media influences our consumer choices and personal/physical self-concept;
Describe differences between healthy bodies and media-generated bodies; and
Produce a media advertisement that promotes the benefits of an active and healthy lifestyle.

units.title: Understands that physical activity provides opportunities for enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and social interaction. Students will:

topics.title: Participate in physical activity:

subtopics.title: Participate in physical activity:

outcomes.text: Identify a variety of physical activities that will provide satisfaction and lead to continued participation;

Choose to participate consistently in games, sports, dance and outdoor activities, both in and out of school, based on individual interests and capabilities (i.e., at school during self-selection times, after-school free time, teams, lessons, family recreation, etc.);
Identify benefits of participating in physical activities throughout one's lifetime (i.e., discussion, lists, outline, role playing, etc.); and
Show a desire to improve one's own physical ability, fitness level and performance (i.e., fitness journals, activity calendars, fitness level assessments, etc).

topics.title: Participate in new and challenging physical activities:

subtopics.title: Participate in new and challenging physical activities:

outcomes.text: Identify opportunities in school and community that encourage/allow for regular participation in physical activity (i.e., community bulletin boards, online searches, class discussions, etc); and
Actively choose and join in on new activities in and out of the school environment (i.e., recess, self-selection times, after-school clubs, family recreation time, etc.).

topics.title: Identify the social benefits of participation in physical activity; grades 5-8 performance standards:

subtopics.title: Identify the social benefits of participation in physical activity; grades 5-8 performance standards:

outcomes.text: Identify basic ideals of fair play, acceptance of rules and group communication (i.e., give appropriate feedback to partners and teammates, etc.);
Appreciate the challenging aspects of competition with self and others (i.e., praise opponents, accept teammates' and opponents' contributions, enjoy physical activity for its own sake, etc.); and

Sharing feelings of satisfaction felt as a result of physical activity (i.e., improved individual self-esteem, good feelings gained from being part of a team, activity journals, class discussions, etc.).

topics.title: Practice and demonstrate physical activity as a vehicle for self expression:

subtopics.title: Practice and demonstrate physical activity as a vehicle for self expression:

outcomes.text: Identify and use a variety of physical activities and movements to communicate ideas and feelings (i.e., dance, sports, gymnastics, intensity levels, etc.);
Demonstrate aesthetic appreciation of skilled movement of the body (i.e., create body silhouettes, etc.);
Identify and describe personal feelings resulting from participation in physical activity (i.e., journals, activity calendars, peer mentoring, class discussions, etc.); and
Exhibit appropriate protocol during dance, fine arts or other physical activity events.
